workflow_rationale: This is a major new feature — transforming mock frontend auth into a full dynamic auth system backed by Frappe endpoints. Requires new backend endpoints, new frontend pages, middleware, custom DocType fields, email templates, and security hardening across two services.

Also added constants: RATE_LIMITS, PASSWORD_REQUIREMENTS, VERIFICATION_CODE_LENGTH, OTP expiry settings. All patterns match identity.py. Uses secrets.randbelow for secure OTP generation, frappe.cache().set_value/delete_value for Redis ops. Verification passed: auth.py compiles. Committed as ba864bb. phases.name: Backend Auth Endpoints
phases.description: Implement all 9 new auth endpoints in auth.py: register, verify_email, resend_verification_otp, login, verify_2fa, forgot_password, verify_reset_otp, reset_password, complete_onboarding. Each endpoint uses rate limiting, input validation, and proper error handling.

subtasks.description: Implement register endpoint: validates email format/uniqueness, password strength, creates Frappe User with custom fields (tradehub_user_type, is_email_verified=0, has_completed_onboarding=0), generates 6-digit OTP, sends verification email. Also implement verify_email endpoint: validates OTP from Redis, marks is_email_verified=1, starts Frappe session, generates auth token, returns user profile. Also implement resend_verification_otp: rate-limited to 60s cooldown per email.

verification.command: cd Frappe_Marketplace/frappe-bench && python -c "from tr_tradehub.api.v1.auth import register, verify_email, resend_verification_otp; print('OK: Registration endpoints importable')" 2>/dev/null || python -m py_compile apps/tr_tradehub/tr_tradehub/api/v1/auth.py && echo 'OK: auth.py compiles with registration endpoints'

subtasks.notes:
Implemented three endpoints in auth.py:

1. register() - @frappe.whitelist(allow_guest=True): validates email format/uniqueness via validate_email_format() and frappe.db.exists(), validates password strength, validates user_type in ('buyer','supplier'), creates Frappe User with custom fields (tradehub_user_type, is_email_verified=0, has_completed_onboarding=0) using hasattr() check for field existence, generates 6-digit OTP via generate_verification_otp(), sends verification email. Cleans up partial user on failure. Rate-limited via check_rate_limit('register').

2. verify_email() - Validates OTP from Redis cache key 'trade_hub:verify:otp:{email}', deletes OTP after success (single-use), clears resend cooldown, marks is_email_verified=1, starts Frappe session via login_manager.login_as(), generates auth token (api_key:api_secret, NOT base64), returns user profile. Rate-limited via check_rate_limit('verification', email).

3. resend_verification_otp() - Enforces 60s cooldown per email via separate Redis key 'trade_hub:verify:cooldown:{email}', checks email not already verified, generates fresh OTP (overwrites previous), sends verification email. Rate-limited via check_rate_limit('verification', email).

Added constants: RESEND_OTP_COOLDOWN_SECONDS=60, VALID_USER_TYPES=('buyer','supplier'). All endpoints use Frappe ORM only (no raw SQL). Verification passed: py_compile succeeds. Committed as 29b2045.

subtasks.description: Implement login endpoint: validates credentials via frappe.utils.password.check_password(), checks if email is verified (if not, sends new OTP and throws with title='email_not_verified'), checks 2FA via should_run_2fa(), handles 2FA flow with custom wrapper (authenticate_for_2factor sets tmp_id in frappe.local.response, store in Redis, return session identifier), on success starts session and returns auth token + user profile.

verification.command: cd Frappe_Marketplace/frappe-bench && python -m py_compile apps/tr_tradehub/tr_tradehub/api/v1/auth.py && echo 'OK: auth.py compiles with login endpoint'
verification.expected: OK: auth.py compiles with login endpoint

subtasks.notes:
Implemented login() endpoint in auth.py with full 2FA support:

1. login() - @frappe.whitelist(allow_guest=True): Rate-limited by IP and email (10/5min). Validates credentials via frappe.utils.password.check_password() with generic error messages to prevent user enumeration. Checks if user is enabled.

2. Email verification check: If is_email_verified=0, generates new OTP via generate_verification_otp(), sends verification email, throws with title='email_not_verified' so frontend can redirect to verify page.

3. 2FA flow: Checks should_run_2fa(email) from frappe.twofactor. If 2FA required: sets frappe.form_dict['pwd'] for caching, calls authenticate_for_2factor(email) which sets tmp_id in frappe.local.response, extracts tmp_id + verification info, generates session_id via secrets.token_urlsafe(32), stores {tmp_id, user} in Redis keyed by 'trade_hub:2fa:session:{session_id}' with 5min expiry, cleans up frappe.local.response, returns session_id + verification method to frontend.

4. Success path (no 2FA): Starts Frappe session via login_manager.login_as(), generates auth token (api_key:api_secret, NOT base64), returns user profile with tradehub custom fields.

All patterns match identity.py and existing endpoints. No raw SQL. Uses Frappe ORM only. Verification passed: py_compile succeeds. Committed as eec42bd.

subtasks.description: Implement verify_2fa endpoint: receives session_id + otp, retrieves tmp_id from Redis, reconstructs LoginManager, calls confirm_otp_token(login_manager, otp, tmp_id), on success starts session and returns auth token + user profile. This is the custom 2FA REST wrapper described in the spec.

verification.command: cd Frappe_Marketplace/frappe-bench && python -m py_compile apps/tr_tradehub/tr_tradehub/api/v1/auth.py && echo 'OK: auth.py compiles with verify_2fa'

subtasks.notes: Implemented verify_2fa endpoint. Receives session_id + otp, retrieves tmp_id from Redis, reconstructs LoginManager via object.__new__(LoginManager), calls confirm_otp_token(login_manager, otp, tmp_id), on success deletes Redis session key, starts Frappe session via login_as(), generates auth token, and returns token + user profile. Rate limited at 5/5min per email. Handles expired sessions, invalid OTP, and JSON parsing errors. Verification passed: py_compile succeeds.

subtasks.description: Implement password reset flow: (1) forgot_password(email) — always returns success message regardless of email existence (anti-enumeration), generates 6-digit OTP, sends password reset email; (2) verify_reset_otp(email, otp) — validates OTP, generates single-use reset_token via secrets.token_urlsafe(32), stores in Redis 10min; (3) reset_password(reset_token, new_password) — validates reset_token from Redis, updates password via frappe update_password(), invalidates token.

verification.command: cd Frappe_Marketplace/frappe-bench && python -m py_compile apps/tr_tradehub/tr_tradehub/api/v1/auth.py && echo 'OK: auth.py compiles with password reset endpoints'
verification.expected: OK: auth.py compiles with password reset endpoints

subtasks.notes:
Implemented three password reset endpoints in auth.py:

1. forgot_password(email) - @frappe.whitelist(allow_guest=True): Rate-limited at 3/hour per email via check_rate_limit('password_reset', email). Anti-enumeration: always returns same success message ("If an account with this email exists, you will receive a password reset code shortly.") regardless of whether email exists. Only generates OTP and sends email for existing, enabled users. Uses generate_password_reset_otp() (6-digit, Redis 15min expiry) and send_password_reset_email().

2. verify_reset_otp(email, otp) - @frappe.whitelist(allow_guest=True): Rate-limited at 5/5min per email via check_rate_limit('verification', email). Validates OTP from Redis key 'trade_hub:reset:otp:{email}', deletes OTP after success (single-use). Generates secure reset_token via secrets.token_urlsafe(32), stores in Redis for 10 minutes at key 'trade_hub:reset:token:{reset_token}' mapping to email. Returns reset_token to frontend.

3. reset_password(reset_token, new_password) - @frappe.whitelist(allow_guest=True): Retrieves email from Redis via reset_token, invalidates token immediately (single-use, deleted before password update), validates user exists and is enabled, validates password strength via validate_password_strength(), updates password via frappe.utils.password.update_password(). User must log in again after successful reset.

Added RESET_TOKEN_EXPIRY_SECONDS = 600 constant. Added import of update_password from frappe.utils.password. All endpoints use Frappe ORM only (no raw SQL). No debugging statements. Verification passed: py_compile succeeds. Committed as ddbfe6b.

subtasks.description: Implement complete_onboarding endpoint: authenticated endpoint (no allow_guest), reads frappe.session.user, sets has_completed_onboarding=1 on User DocType, returns success with redirect URL. Simple endpoint but important for middleware redirect logic.

verification.command: cd Frappe_Marketplace/frappe-bench && python -m py_compile apps/tr_tradehub/tr_tradehub/api/v1/auth.py && echo 'OK: auth.py compiles with complete_onboarding'

subtasks.notes: Implemented complete_onboarding endpoint: authenticated (@frappe.whitelist() without allow_guest), reads frappe.session.user, validates user exists and is not Guest, sets has_completed_onboarding=1 via frappe.db.set_value, determines redirect URL based on tradehub_user_type (supplier -> supplier-dashboard, buyer -> buyer-dashboard), returns success with redirect_url. Includes proper error handling with frappe.log_error. Verification passed: auth.py compiles. Committed as a476309. Phase 2 (Backend Auth Endpoints) is now fully complete.

phases.name: Security Hardening & Integration
phases.description: Comprehensive security audit of all auth endpoints and end-to-end integration verification. Verify rate limiting, CSRF protection, input validation, no raw SQL, XSS prevention, token security, and cross-tab logout. Run through all auth flows to verify they work end-to-end.

subtasks.description: Security audit of all backend auth endpoints: (1) Verify check_rate_limit() is called at the START of every auth endpoint; (2) Verify zero occurrences of frappe.db.sql() in auth.py auth functions; (3) Verify all user inputs are validated server-side (email format, password strength); (4) Verify OTP single-use enforcement (delete_value after verification); (5) Verify reset_token single-use enforcement; (6) Verify forgot_password returns same success message for existing and non-existing emails (anti-enumeration); (7) Verify no password or sensitive data in any response payload or logs.

verification.instructions: Code review of auth.py focusing on: (1) grep for 'frappe.db.sql' — must be zero matches in auth functions. (2) Verify each @frappe.whitelist endpoint starts with check_rate_limit(). (3) Verify delete_value() used after every OTP/token validation. (4) Verify forgot_password response is identical for found/not-found emails. (5) Verify no 'password' key in any return dict.

subtasks.notes: Security audit of all backend auth endpoints completed. Fixed 4 issues: (1) verify_2fa missing IP-based rate limit at start + missing OTP format validation, (2) reset_password missing rate limiting entirely, (3) check_email_exists missing rate limiting for anti-enumeration, (4) check_email_exists missing email format validation. All 7 audit criteria verified: zero frappe.db.sql(), rate limiting on all auth endpoints, OTP single-use enforcement, reset_token single-use, anti-enumeration on forgot_password, no password in responses/logs.

subtasks.description: Frontend security verification: (1) Verify all fetch() calls include credentials:'include'; (2) Verify token format is 'token api_key:api_secret' (lowercase, no base64); (3) Verify CSRF token sent on POST requests; (4) Verify DOMPurify used on any user-generated content; (5) Verify loading/disabled states on all submit buttons (prevent double submission); (6) Verify reset_token stored in component state only (not localStorage); (7) Verify cross-tab logout via storage event listener; (8) Verify middleware redirects work correctly.

verification.instructions: Code review of all modified frontend files focusing on: (1) grep for 'fetch(' — verify credentials:'include' present. (2) grep for 'Authorization' — verify 'token ' prefix (lowercase). (3) Verify reset_token not in localStorage. (4) Verify all buttons have loading state during API calls. (5) Verify storage event listener for cross-tab logout.

subtasks.notes:
Frontend security verification complete. All 8 criteria verified:
1. ✅ credentials:'include' on all fetch() calls (api.ts apiGet/apiPost)
2. ✅ Token format 'token api_key:api_secret' (lowercase, no base64)
3. ✅ CSRF token X-Frappe-CSRF-Token on POST requests via buildHeaders(true)
4. ✅ XSS prevention — FIXED: added escapeHtml() to EmailVerification.ts maskEmail() to prevent innerHTML XSS injection
5. ✅ Loading/disabled states on all submit buttons across LoginPage, RegisterPage, ForgotPasswordPage, VerifyPage, WelcomePage
6. ✅ reset_token in Alpine component state only (not localStorage), cleared after use and on destroy()
7. ✅ Cross-tab logout via storage event listener in middleware.ts for 'tradehub_tokens' key
8. ✅ Middleware redirects correct — FIXED: added isSafeReturnUrl() to LoginPage.ts to prevent open-redirect via ?return= query parameter

subtasks.description: End-to-end integration verification: Verify all auth flows work when both services are running. Test: (1) Registration flow — register, receive OTP, verify, land on welcome. (2) Login flow — email/password, get tokens, redirect to dashboard. (3) Login with unverified email — redirect to verify page. (4) Password reset flow — request, verify OTP, set new password, login. (5) Middleware — unauthenticated redirect to login, onboarding redirect to welcome. (6) Logout — clears tokens and server session. (7) Social login buttons call correct SSO endpoints. (8) Existing Keycloak SSO still works alongside new endpoints.

steps: Start backend: cd Frappe_Marketplace/frappe-bench && bench start
Start frontend: cd tradehubfront && npm run dev
Navigate to http://localhost:5173/pages/auth/login.html — verify login with email/password
Navigate to http://localhost:5173/pages/welcome.html — verify onboarding wizard
Verify protected page redirect: navigate to buyer-dashboard without auth → should redirect to login
Verify existing SSO endpoints still respond: GET /api/method/tr_tradehub.api.v1.auth.get_sso_status

subtasks.notes: End-to-end integration verification complete. Found and fixed 8 critical integration bugs: (1) LoginPage/VerifyPage/2FA response type mismatch — frontend expected flat api_key/api_secret but backend nests under token:{}, causing silent login failure; (2) FrappeError class added to preserve error title from _server_messages, fixing email_not_verified redirect detection; (3) All dashboard redirect paths fixed to actual existing pages (buyer-dashboard.html, sell.html); (4) BackendUser→AuthUser mapping added for field name differences (is_email_verified→is_verified, number→boolean); (5) Token refresh null-safety prevents localStorage corruption; (6) Logout now calls backend API to invalidate server session; (7) Backend complete_onboarding redirect paths fixed; (8) handleLoginError updated to check FrappeError.title for email_not_verified. All 21/21 subtasks now complete.

parallel_groups.reason: Both depend only on phase-1-backend-foundation, different services (backend vs frontend), no file conflicts

Phase 5 depends only on phase-3, phase 4 depends on phase-2+3. Phase 5 creates new files while phase 4 modifies existing ones, so no conflicts. However phase 4 and 5 both modify Alpine auth.ts, so conservative recommendation is sequential.

parallelism.speedup_estimate: 1.4x faster than sequential — Phase 2 (5 subtasks) and Phase 3 (4 subtasks) run in parallel, saving ~40% of the middle phase time

acceptance_criteria: All new auth endpoints respond correctly
No raw SQL queries in auth code (Frappe ORM only)
Rate limiting enforced on all auth endpoints
CSRF tokens sent on all POST requests
Token format is 'token api_key:api_secret' (lowercase, no base64)
No passwords or sensitive data in API responses

verification_steps.name: Rate Limit Coverage
verification_steps.expected_outcome: At least 6 rate limit calls (one per auth endpoint)

verification_strategy.reasoning: Authentication is the highest-security surface. This task touches login, registration, password reset, 2FA, token management, session handling, and CSRF protection across both frontend and backend. Critical risk level demands comprehensive security scanning, unit+integration+E2E tests, and staging verification.
